title: Bonds Fixing Failing & Aging Infrastructure; Improving Safety, Vocational Facilities
ballot_label: Bonds Fixing Failing & Aging Infrastructure; Improving Safety, Vocational Facilities. Shall District issue bonds to increase safety, security, repair aging schools and failing infrastructure, expand vocational classrooms, secure matching funds? If the bonds are approved, they will be payable from taxes on property or property ownership that are not subject to the limits of sections 11 and 11b, Article XI of the Oregon Constitution.
summary: Hillsboro School District No. 1J asks voters to approve $430 million in general obligation bonds for capital costs, including repairs to aging buildings and systems, safety and security upgrades, expanded career and technical education classrooms, and other projects. The ballot summary estimates a levy rate of $1.84 per $1,000 of assessed value, says the district would be eligible for $6.1 million in state matching funds, and requires a community oversight committee and regular audits.
yes_means: A yes vote approves the district issuing $430 million in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes outside the constitutional limits, for school repairs, safety and security, and vocational facilities.
no_means: A no vote rejects the district issuing these general obligation bonds and the associated property tax.
fiscal_impact: Per the ballot summary: principal amount $430 million; estimated levy rate $1.84 per $1,000 of assessed value; bonds may be issued in multiple series, each maturing within 21 years; district eligible for $6.1 million in state matching funds if passed.

gaps: Ten arguments in favor were filed in the Washington County voters' pamphlet (WC-60 to WC-64, counting the Spanish-language School Board argument). The 6-per-side cap is filled with the first six in pamphlet order; not itemized: Hillsboro parents (Briana Ellenberger, WC-63); extracurriculars/athletics (Patrick Maguire, WC-63); community leaders and HSD Budget Committee representatives (Kim Strelchun, WC-64); Fire Science graduates (Katie Rhyne, WC-64).
The Multnomah County pamphlet (M-98) prints this measure with 'No arguments in favor of or opposition to this measure were filed'; arguments appear only in the Washington County edition.

collection_notes: Updated 2026-10-16 from the Washington County voters' pamphlet extract (WC-59 ballot title and explanatory statement; WC-60 to WC-65 arguments: 10 in favor, 2 in opposition) and the Multnomah County extract (M-98, no arguments printed). The first yes argument is printed in English and Spanish columns; the Spanish column has different signers and furnisher so it is counted as a separate filed argument. Both arguments in opposition are by Jason Williams, Taxpayers Association of Oregon, printed in two columns on WC-65. Oregon local ballot titles have no official result-of-vote text; yes_means/no_means are neutral one-sentence descriptions written by the collector strictly from the official ballot caption/question. Ballot caption, question and summary facts were taken from the Multnomah County sample ballot for Nov 3, 2026 (multco.us, T1), because the Washington County ballot-title PDF is a scanned image; the caption matches the Washington County current-election listing and inventory.json exactly. The ballot_label was assembled from consecutive verbatim quotes returned by WebFetch (the tool caps single quotes), so a verifier should confirm it against the PDF. Jurisdiction and number match the inventory; multco.us lists the filing date as 8/27/2026. District pages say the board voted unanimously on May 26, 2026 to refer the bond. Per-side T3 searches found no attributed YES or NO statements; KPTV (May 28, 2026, FOX 12 Staff) reports only district figures. The session-wide WebSearch budget ran out before the final per-side '"Measure <number>" <jurisdiction>' search could be run; the allowed_domains T3 search was rejected by the search proxy (HTTP 400) on every attempt, so T3 coverage relies on plain searches. Outlet-specific follow-up searches were not possible.
